measures.title: Increasing the Timeframe for the Hawaii Senate to Consider and Act on Judicial Appointments
measures.summary: This legislatively proposed amendment would give the State Senate 60 days instead of 30 to confirm or reject the Governor's appointments of Supreme Court, Intermediate Court of Appeals and circuit court judges when the appointment is made between April 1 and December 31, typically when the Legislature is adjourning or out of session. Today, the Senate is deemed to consent if it does not act within 30 days, which can force special sessions just for judicial appointments. To pass, an amendment needs a majority of yes/no votes that is also at least 50% of all ballots cast, so a blank vote has the same effect as a no vote.
measures.yesMeans: The Senate would have 60 days, instead of 30, to act on judicial appointments made between April 1 and December 31.
measures.noMeans: The Constitution is unchanged, and the Senate keeps 30 days to act on a judicial appointment or is deemed to have consented.

measures.title: Directing the Hawaii State Legislature to Establish Procedures for Counties to Issue RISE Bonds, Exempt from County Debt Limits
measures.summary: This legislatively proposed amendment would direct the Legislature to let counties issue a new type of bond, resilient infrastructure for shelter and equity (RISE) bonds, to pay for public improvements in designated districts. The bonds would be repaid only from future growth in property tax revenue in those districts, not by raising property tax rates, and would not count toward a county's debt limit. To pass, an amendment needs a majority of yes/no votes that is also at least 50% of all ballots cast, so a blank vote has the same effect as a no vote.
measures.yesMeans: The Legislature would set up laws letting counties issue RISE bonds, excluded from county debt limits and repaid only from future property tax growth in the districts they help develop.
measures.noMeans: The Constitution is unchanged, and counties could not issue RISE bonds.
